ground.credit: WATER: SENTINEL-2 · 28 AUGUST 2025 · CONTAINS MODIFIED COPERNICUS SENTINEL DATA 2025 · HATCHED, THE RESERVOIR ON 5 JUNE 2023 · LINES: OPENSTREETMAP CONTRIBUTORS

water.rule: water: clear pixels with MNDWI over 0.2 (green against SWIR) and NIR reflectance under 15%; or SWIR under 11% and under 0.6 of the median round it (31 px), MNDWI over -0.25 (water in a pixel shared with plants: the narrow channels); runs under 6 px dropped, inside the bed's footprint; the edge softened (1.2 px)
water.drawn: resampled onto the frame (bilinear), filled a shade darker and outlined

old_water.what: the 3D bed's footprint: the water on the last clear pass before the dam was destroyed (Sentinel-2, 5 June 2023; bed.json `reference`)
old_water.drawn: hatched light at 45 degrees (18 px apart at 3840 px, 0.42 strong), its shore outlined faintly

areas_drawn: each area outlined in its own colour (AREA_RGB), semi-transparent, no fill; its label lists each repair's date (the date its source gives for the work or the reconnection)

centres.drawn: a small cross at each area's centre (of the area as drawn; on the area when a bent band's centre falls outside it): marks the area, so overlapping areas can be told apart and counted; never a place of work, a tower or a crew

lines.source: OpenStreetMap power=line ways traced in network.json (ODbL)
lines.drawn: plain, in the zoom-out's two yellows (750 kV the brighter), fading toward their ends; no state: the still has no date

rule.text: Where lines were damaged or repaired, or crews sent, only as a general region: a stretch of line or an area at least about 3 km across, never finer than the source; never a tower, a pin, coordinates or a crew's position; never the Dniprovska substation's place or the trench site (CLAUDE.md; NEXT.md I5)

how_drawn: Each repair whose place was published lays one translucent white layer over the area its source names, so the areas where crews went again and again are brighter: accumulated. An area along a line is the line's stretch (OpenStreetMap, network.json) widened to a band 3 km wide with rounded ends; its sides and banks are those the unrolled film uses (the shores of 5 June 2023 and the channel of September 2023, from the 3D survey's water masks: the channel taken as the front). The area round the switchyards is a circle round both switchyards' OpenStreetMap outlines, widened by 0.6 km. Every edge is dashed: an area, not a point. Drawn, not observed; never a tower, a pin or a crew.

caveats: Accumulated only as far as the sources go: 21 repairs or restorations had no place published, and others may not have been reported at all. An area with fewer layers is not one with fewer repairs, only fewer whose place was published. Most published places are for Ferosplavna-1 and the switchyards because the IAEA began giving places from late 2022 and named them often only for the ceasefires (from October 2025).

The other seven lines (Zaporizka, Pivdennodonbaska and Kakhovska 750 kV; Zaporizka, Molochanska, Melitopolska and Kakhovska 330 kV): no completed repair found after they were cut in 2022, only Rosatom's plans and work in progress (R14). They are drawn, without areas, because none were placed, not because none were tried.

The IAEA's own ceasefire numbering differs from the unrolled film's (config networks.znpp.unrolled.truces): its third is the December 2025 repair of the plant-to-thermal-plant link (R39), its fourth Ferosplavna-1 in January 2026 at 'approximately 10 kilometres from the ZTPP 330 kV open switchyard' (R40, the unrolled film says no place published), its fifth the link at the thermal plant's switchyard in February-March 2026 (R41, which the unrolled film draws as Ferosplavna-1 with no place). Left for the user: the unrolled config is unchanged.

R21's dates disagree (Ukrenergo: repaired 24-25 February 2024; the IAEA and the ministry: restored 14 March). R44's place disagrees (the IAEA: near the thermal plant's switchyard; OECD-NEA: a substation north of the river).
Who repaired on the Russian-held side is mostly unpublished (R35d, R36, R39, R44, R45b); R41 is credited to Rosatom by a Russian outlet only.
